advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Reconcile ADR 0102's check_repo_root_agreement claim with snapshot.py (either wire the guard into snapshot consumption or drop/soften the ADR statement).
evidence: ADR text: 'the snapshot carries `repo_root` as its own frozen field and `check_repo_root_agreement` guards mismatches'
check_repo_root_agreement is defined at src/rebar/llm/criteria/overlay.py:112 but unused by the snapshot module
advisory.finding: ADR 0102 asserts the snapshot's repo-root binding is guarded by check_repo_root_agreement ('the snapshot carries repo_root as its own frozen field and check_repo_root_agreement guards mismatches'), but snapshot.py never calls check_repo_root_agreement — the guard described in the ADR is not wired into compile_snapshot or CriteriaSnapshot.
scenarios: A reader trusts the ADR that repo-root mismatches are guarded when consuming a snapshot compiled against a different repo_root.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test asserting two distinct repo_roots with byte-identical overlays (and two overlay-absent roots) produce equal digests, guarding ADR 0102's content-fingerprint contract.
evidence: ADR 0102: 'two repositories whose effective overlays are byte-identical (or both absent) share a digest, which is the intended semantics'

test_digest_is_deterministic_and_content_bound uses root_a (cr_globs=["**"]) recompiled for determinism and root_b (cr_globs=["src/**"]) for divergence — both about a single repo's content, never two distinct repos with identical content
snapshot.py:274-277: digest = sha256(signature + payload); signature is content-only (overlay.py:154-164) and payload is routing-only, so cross-repo equality is a real but unguarded property
advisory.finding: ADR 0102's explicit digest contract — 'two repositories whose effective overlays are byte-identical (or both absent) share a digest' — is untested. test_digest_is_deterministic_and_content_bound only proves same-repo determinism and different-content divergence; no test compiles two DIFFERENT repo_roots with byte-identical overlays (or two overlay-absent roots) and asserts equal digests, so a regression that folds repo_root into the digest would pass unnoticed.
scenarios: A future change that mixes repo_root into _canonical_routing_payload or the digest input would break the ADR-declared content-fingerprint semantics with no failing test.
advisory.suggested_fix: Add: compile two repos under separate tmp_path dirs with the same _overlay(cr_globs=["**"]) and assert equal digests; also assert compile_snapshot(None)-equivalent absent-overlay repos share a digest.

dropped.checklist_item: - [ ] Confirm the precheck should validate applies_to for non-activated code_review project entries, or scope it to activated ids to match _compile_gate's active loop.
evidence: _precheck iterates `for cid, entry in gate_map.items():` over the raw code_review map with no activation check
The second loop in _compile_gate iterates only `active = overlay.effective_criteria(...)` (activated ids), showing the intended active set is narrower than the precheck set
overlay.effective_criteria only adds project ids whose activation opts into the gate (overlay.py:433-451)
dropped.finding: _precheck_code_review_applies_to validates the strict non-empty applies_to rule against EVERY project.-prefixed non-DET entry present in the raw code_review overlay map, including criteria that are not activated (absent from `activate`). effective_criteria only activates ids listed in `activate`, so a present-but-inactive code-review project LLM entry with a bad applies_to is rejected at snapshot compile even though it would never run.
scenarios: An overlay declares a code_review project LLM criterion with a malformed applies_to but leaves it out of `activate` intending it inert.
